title: Book Three · Chapter 41: The Wide Window
story:
On Monday after school, Anna walks slowly down the stairs.

“Still your legs?” Ronan asks.

“A little. The stairs know.”

Her friend has gone ahead to meet someone. Kai has a game with the boys. Ronan and Anna reach the gate together.

Anna looks down the road.

“I want to see the hall window again.”

“The wide one?”

“Yes. Have you got time?”

He has some school work at home, but not a whole evening of it.

“For a little while.”

They walk to the public hall. The big front doors are open. A few people sit inside, but Anna stops at the wall outside.

Above it, the wide window throws light across the entrance floor. She takes a notebook from her bag.

“I tried to draw it from memory,” she says.

The drawing has three tall shapes. The real window has four.

“It grew,” Ronan says.

“Or I lost a part.”

She sits on the low wall. Ronan sits beside her, with a little space between them.

Anna studies the window and adds another line. Then she looks at the doorway below it.

“People can see the step clearly in there.”

Ronan follows her finger. Light falls along the edge of the first step.

A man carries a chair through the doorway. He turns it sideways at the step. Anna watches the chair pass, then marks the narrow side of the door on her page.

“Even on a grey day?” he asks.

“I want to see that too.”

A woman comes out with two bags. Ronan moves his feet to give her room. Anna pulls her notebook closer to her knees.

When the woman passes, Anna gives Ronan the pencil.

“Your turn.”

“A whole window?”

“One door. Start small.”

He draws two long sides and a line across the top. The door leans a little.

Anna looks at it.

“Where does it open?”

He adds a handle in the middle.

She laughs. “Two hands?”

“A strong door.”

He moves the handle to one side. Anna leans across to look, and their shoulders touch.

For a moment, she stays there. Ronan can feel the warmth through his shirt.

Then she sits straight and takes the pencil back. He looks at the wide window again. Neither says anything for a little while.

“I should go,” he says at last.

“Me too.”

At the corner, their roads part. Anna closes the notebook with both drawings inside.

“Next grey day,” she says.

“For the window?”

“Yes. Bring a better door.”

Ronan smiles and turns toward West Lane.

At home, Mum asks him to move his bag from her chair. He does, then opens his school book at the table.

His first line is crooked. He rubs it out and starts again.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

public hall＝公共会堂；from memory＝凭记忆；lean＝倾斜；give someone room＝给别人让出空间。

## 理解问题

1. Anna为什么想再看一次会堂的窗？她观察的不只是窗户数量，还包括什么？
2. 两人在矮墙旁怎样一起画画？最后有没有因此放弃各自回家的安排？

## 读句子

**He moves the handle to one side.**

拆开看：He / moves the handle / to one side.

他／把画中的门把手移过去／移到一侧。
